raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

I've been farming this land for 25 years now, so I know what to expect. My 60 mu is split up — about 40 mu is wheat-maize rotation on the better ground closer to the well, and 20 mu I keep in cotton because that land dried out worse in 2019 and cotton handles it better. That's how my father did it too, and changing the layout now would just be trouble.

**Wheat** goes in around October 10th, after the autumn rains settle the ground. I use the Jimai variety — I bought fresh seed two seasons back and I've been saving some, but this year I'll buy new again because yield was dropping a bit. Before planting I spread about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu as base, that gives me roughly 6 kg of N from that. Then at jointing in March I topdress 25 kg of urea per mu, so altogether I'm putting down about 17-18 kg N per mu. The extension station guy says 15 is enough but I always add a bit more — last year the field at the east edge where I skimped a little came out 50 kg lighter. Not worth saving 20 yuan to lose that.

I irrigate wheat 3 times if the weather is normal — once before winter to lock in moisture, once at jointing with the topdressing, and once around heading in early May. If May is dry I'll do a fourth. Water from the well costs about 25 yuan per mu per irrigation with electricity and everything, so I watch the sky before I pump. Herbicide goes on in early spring for the weeds, and I spray once at heading if I see aphids. I'm aiming for about 450 kg per mu — that's what I got the last two years, no reason to expect different.

**Maize** follows wheat immediately. That's the hard part — I need to get it in within about 5-6 days after the wheat combine, so I don't till, I just use the no-till planter I rent from my cousin for 15 yuan per mu. Zhengdan 958 is what most people around here grow and I stick with it, seed costs about 45 yuan per mu. I apply one round of compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg per mu, and if the maize looks pale at the big trumpet stage (around late July) I'll topdress another 15-20 kg of urea. Total N ends up around 15 kg per mu. I only irrigate maize if July-August is dry — usually 1 or 2 times, sometimes zero if the summer rains come. Herbicide right after planting is a must, and I keep an eye out for borers. Yield target about 500 kg per mu.

**Cotton** I plant around April 20th on the 20 mu west of the house. It's Lumianyan seed, I buy certified seed every year because cotton seed quality really matters. Cotton I fertilize lighter — about 12-13 kg N per mu, split between base and one topdressing at flowering. It's pesticide-heavy though, I spray 5-6 times through the season for bollworm and aphids. Irrigation once or twice during flowering if it's dry. The real work with cotton is the picking — three rounds by hand from September through late October. My wife and I can't do it all, so I hire 4-5 people from the village for maybe 15-20 days. That's the biggest cost for cotton, but the price has held up okay, so I keep 20 mu in it. Yield around 250 kg of lint per mu is what I plan for.

My older son works in Handan during the week so I only have him for harvests. My daughter is still in school. So it's mostly me and my wife doing the daily work, with hired help at cotton picking and some machine operators I hire for the wheat combine and maize planter.

Total cash I'll spend on inputs is somewhere around 36,000-38,000 yuan. That's tight but manageable — I always keep 5,000 yuan back in case something goes wrong.
